arxiv-2109-05095.title: Stochastic Adversarial Koopman Model for Dynamical Systems
arxiv-2109-05095.creator: Kaushik Balakrishnan, Devesh Upadhyay
arxiv-2109-05095.description: Abstract Dynamical systems are ubiquitous and are often modeled using a non-linear system of governing equations. Numerical solution procedures for many dynamical systems have existed for several decades, but can be slow due to high-dimensional state space of the dynamical system.

arxiv-2211-12503.title: Is the Elephant Flying? Resolving Ambiguities in Text-to-Image Generative Models
arxiv-2211-12503.creator: Ninareh Mehrabi *1 , Palash Goyal 2 , Apurv Verma 2 , Jwala Dhamala 2 , Varun Kumar 2 , Qian Hu 2 , Kai-Wei Chang 2 , Richard Zemel 2 , Aram Galstyan 2 , Rahul Gupta 2
arxiv-2211-12503.description: Abstract Natural language often contains ambiguities that can lead to misinterpretation and miscommunication. While humans can handle ambiguities effectively by asking clarifying questions and/or relying on contextual cues and common-sense knowledge, resolving ambiguities can be notoriously hard for machines. In this work, we study ambiguities that arise in text-to-image generative models.

arxiv-2302-05425.title: Deep Learning Based Object Tracking in Walking Droplet and Granular Intruder Experiments Thanks: Department of Mechanical Engineering, University of Washington Thanks: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, University of Washington
arxiv-2302-05425.creator: Erdi Kara, George Zhang, Joseph J. Williams, Gonzalo Ferrandez-Quinto
arxiv-2302-05425.description: Abstract We present a deep-learning based tracking objects of interest in walking droplet and granular intruder experiments. In a typical walking droplet experiment, a liquid droplet, known as walker , propels itself laterally on the free surface of a vibrating bath of the same liquid.

arxiv-2311-11639.title: Efficient learning of sparse Pauli-Lindblad models for fully connected qubit topology
arxiv-2311-11639.creator: Jose Este Jaloveckas, Minh Tham Pham Nguyen, Lilly Palackal, Jeanette Miriam Lorenz, Hans Ehm
arxiv-2311-11639.description: Abstract The challenge to achieve practical quantum computing considering current hardware size and gate fidelity is the sensitivity to errors and noise. Recent work has shown that by learning the underlying noise model capturing qubit cross-talk, error mitigation can push the boundary of practical quantum computing.

arxiv-2403-08006.title: Quantum tunneling of the magnetization in systems with anisotropic 4f ion pairs: Rates from low temperature zero field relaxation
arxiv-2403-08006.creator: Thomas Greber
arxiv-2403-08006.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Thomas Greber. Anisotropic open shell 4f ions have magnetic moments that can be read and written as atomic bits. If it comes to qbits where the phase of the wave function has to be written, controlled and read, it is of advantage to rely on more than one atom that carries the quantum information of the system because states with different susceptibilities may be addressed.

arxiv-2404-18039.title: Implicit Update of the Moment Equations for a Multi-Species, Homogeneous BGK Model Thanks: This manuscript has been authored, in part, by UT-Battelle, LLC, under contract DE-AC05-00OR22725 with the US Department of Energy (DOE). The U.S. government retains and the publisher, by accepting the article
arxiv-2404-18039.creator: Evan Habbershaw, Cory D. Hauck, Steven M. Wise
arxiv-2404-18039.description: Abstract A simple iterative approach for solving a set of implicit kinetic moment equations is proposed. This implicit solve is a key component in the IMEX discretization of the multi-species Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (M-BGK) model with nontrivial collision frequencies depending on individual species temperatures. We prove that under mild time step restrictions, the iterative method generates a contraction mapping.

arxiv-2405-16151.title: Moderate deviation principles for the WASEP Thanks: Acknowledgments. The project is supported by the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities in China, and by the National Natural Science Foundation of China with grant numbers 11971038 and 12371142.
arxiv-2405-16151.creator: Linjie Zhao
arxiv-2405-16151.description: Abstract . We study the weakly asymmetric simple exclusion process on the integer lattice. Under suitable constraints on the strength of the weak asymmetry of the dynamics, we prove moderate deviation principles for the fluctuation fields when the process starts from stationary measures.

arxiv-2406-00025.title: SCALM: Towards Semantic Caching for Automated Chat Services with Large Language Models
arxiv-2406-00025.creator: Jiaxing Li, Chi Xu, Feng Wang, Isaac M von Riedemann, Cong Zhang, Jiangchuan Liu
arxiv-2406-00025.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have become increasingly popular, transforming a wide range of applications across various domains. However, the real-world effectiveness of their query cache systems has not been thoroughly investigated. In this work, we for the first time conducted an analysis on real-world human-to-LLM interaction data, identifying key challenges in existing caching solutions for LLM-based chat services.

arxiv-2503-05581.title: Constraining the Scattered Light properties of LTT 9779 b Using HST/WFC3 UVIS
arxiv-2503-05581.creator: Michael Radica, Jake Taylor, Hannah R. Wakeford, David Lafrenière, Romain Allart, Nicolas B. Cowan, James S. Jenkins, Vivien Parmentier
arxiv-2503-05581.description: Abstract A planet’s albedo is a fundamental property that sets its energy budget by dictating the fraction of incident radiation absorbed versus reflected back to space. Generally, optical eclipse observations have revealed the majority of hot, giant planets to have low albedos, indicating dayside atmospheres dominated by absorption instead of reflection.

arxiv-2505-06920.title: Bi-directional Self-Registration for Misaligned Infrared-Visible Image Fusion
arxiv-2505-06920.creator: Timing Li, Bing Cao, Pengfei Zhu, Bin Xiao, Qinghua Hu
arxiv-2505-06920.description: Abstract Acquiring accurately aligned multi-modal image pairs is fundamental for achieving high-quality multi-modal image fusion. To address the lack of ground truth in current multi-modal image registration and fusion methods, we propose a novel self-supervised B i-directional S elf- R egistration framework ( B-SR ).

arxiv-2511-02808.title: Reliable Parameter Inference for the Epoch of Reionization using Balanced Neural Ratio Estimation
arxiv-2511-02808.creator: Diego González-Hernández, Molly Wolfson, Joseph F. Hennawi
arxiv-2511-02808.description: Abstract We present an application of the Balanced Neural Ratio Estimation (BNRE) algorithm to improve the statistical validity of parameter estimates used to characterize the Epoch of Reionization, where the common assumption of a multivariate Gaussian likelihood leads to overconfident and biased posterior distributions.

pmc-10495164.title: Utility of routine postoperative chest radiography in patients undergoing clavicle fixation: a retrospective chart review
pmc-10495164.creator: Joshua Del Papa, Josh Hobson, Steve Mann
pmc-10495164.description: Background:Although uncommon, pneumothorax is a potentially serious complication following open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of clavicle fractures. In many centres it is routine practice to obtain postoperative chest radiographs following ORIF of clavicle fractures to assess for iatrogenic pneumothorax.

pmc-10604559.title: Paraoxonase 2 Deficiency Causes Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Retinal Pigment Epithelial Cells and Retinal Degeneration in Mice
pmc-10604559.creator: Parameswaran Gangadharan Sreekumar, Feng Su, Christine Spee, Elise Hong, Ravikiran Komirisetty, Eduardo Araujo, Steven Nusinowitz, Srinivasa T. Reddy, Ram Kannan
pmc-10604559.description: Although AMD is a complex disease, oxidative stress is a crucial contributor to its development, especially in view of the higher oxygen demand of the retina. Paraoxonase 2 (PON2) is a ubiquitously and constitutively expressed antioxidant protein that is found intracellularly associated with mitochondrial membranes and modulates mitochondrial ROS production and function.

pmc-11456821.title: Self-supervised in-domain representation learning for remote sensing image scene classification
pmc-11456821.creator: Ali Ghanbarzadeh, Hossein Soleimani
pmc-11456821.description: Transferring the ImageNet pre-trained weights to the various remote sensing tasks has produced acceptable results and reduced the need for labeled samples. However, the domain differences between ground imageries and remote sensing images cause the performance of such transfer learning to be limited.

pmc-11643410.title: Laccase Production Optimization from Recombinant E. coli BL21 Codon Plus Containing Novel Laccase Gene from Bacillus megaterium for Removal of Wastewater Textile Dye
pmc-11643410.creator: Zannara Mustafa, Ikram ul Haq, Ali Nawaz, Abdulrahman H Alessa, Muhammad Nauman Aftab, Ahmad A Alsaigh, Aziz ur Rehman, Danuta Wojcieszyńska
pmc-11643410.description: The aim of the present research was the efficient degradation of industrial textile wastewater dyes using a very active cloned laccase enzyme. For this purpose, potent laccase-producing bacteria were isolated from soil samples collected from wastewater-replenished textile sites in Punjab, Pakistan.

pmc-12589883.title: Flavivirus-based bivalent nanoparticle vaccines induce neutralizing antibodies and Th1 responses against flavivirus and coupling antigens
pmc-12589883.creator: Koga Ii, Fumitaka Sato, Yu Hatakeyama, Hidehiko Suzuki, Takafumi Noguchi, Kotaro Ishida, Masashi Arakawa, Kazumasa Nakamura, Ryuta Iwatsuki, Cong Thanh Nguyen, Akiho Yoshida, Nobuyuki Tanaka, Ikuo Tsunoda, Hirotaka Ebina, Eiji Morita
pmc-12589883.description: SummaryEffective vaccines against flaviviruses, including Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), are widely used. We developed antigen-loaded nanoparticle vaccines, using JEV virus-like particles (JEV-VLPs) as carriers. The severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike receptor-binding domain (S-RBD) was covalently coupled to specific peptide insertion sites on the JEV envelope protein.

pmc-12642069.title: Research on the driving paths of farmers’ participation in physical activity and its impact on well-being
pmc-12642069.creator: Haixia Wang, Qiuying Li, Bin Gu, Laibing Lu
pmc-12642069.description: “Driving paths” refer to typical combinations of mechanisms formed by the joint influence of multiple socio-ecological factors that motivate individuals to engage in specific behaviors (such as physical exercise). Exploring the driving paths of farmers’ participation in physical exercise holds significant importance for enhancing their engagement in physical activity and improving their well-being.

pmc-12986064.title: Advances in Membrane, Dialyzer Design, and Related Monitoring Technologies for Hemodiafiltration: Translating Bench-Side Innovations to Bedside Applications
pmc-12986064.creator: Alfred Gagel, Gerhard Wiesen, Stefano Stuard, Bernard Canaud
pmc-12986064.description: Background: Online hemodiafiltration (HDF) represents the most advanced form of kidney replacement therapy, combining diffusive and convective transport to enhance the removal of uremic toxins across a wide molecular spectrum. Achieving high convective volumes is a key determinant of treatment efficacy and has been associated with improved survival.

pmc-13093778.title: Unveiling the immune landscape and microenvironmental architecture of IgA nephropathy using single‐cell imaging mass cytometry
pmc-13093778.creator: Xing Chen, Long Liu, Lijing Yao, Jianxin Shen, Hengyuan Zhang, Leping Shao, Xingxing Yu, Zhijuan Lin, Lu Zhang
pmc-13093778.description: ObjectiveThe heterogeneity in the pathology of IgA nephropathy (IgAN) represents a significant gap in current research, emphasising the need for individualised treatment strategies. The role of the glomerular microenvironment in driving IgAN heterogeneity remains largely unknown.MethodsThis study employed Imaging Mass Cytometry (IMC) to analyse 34 primary IgAN renal biopsies.

pmc-13219639.title: A novel hybrid deep learning framework for customer churn prediction using RFM and embedding clustering
pmc-13219639.creator: Samia Ibrahim, BenBella S. Tawfik, Mohamed Abdallah Makhlouf, B. Hafiz
pmc-13219639.description: Customer churn prediction in E-commerce remains a challenging task due to the lack of labeled data, and the limited ability of traditional machine learning models to capture complex and dynamic customer behavior patterns. Existing approaches either rely on handcrafted features without effective representation learning or apply deep learning models without incorporating meaningful customer segmentation.

pmc-13223191.title: Study on mmage defect recognition and classification of power transmission equipment based on lightweight model residual Mamba
pmc-13223191.creator: Cui Jindong, Song Weijie, Guan Shan, Sun Liang, Tian Hongliang, Wang Fuwang
pmc-13223191.description: Image defect detection of power transmission and transformation equipment is a key technology in the operation and maintenance of power systems, which is of vital importance for ensuring the safe and stable operation of the power grid and enhancing its self-healing capacity.

pmc-13376590.title: Dapagliflozin Augmentation of Sacubitril/Valsartan Therapy in Patients With Heart Failure Following PCI‐Treated Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Meta‐Analysis of Clinical Efficacy and Safety
pmc-13376590.creator: Tang Tang, Huimin Yu, Yun Zhang, Shuang Li, Mu Guo
pmc-13376590.description: PurposeTo systematically review the efficacy and safety of dapagliflozin and sacubitril/valsartan (SV) in patients with heart failure (HF) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)–treated acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and to provide evidence for clinical practice.MethodsSeven electronic databases were systematically searched from their inception to July 25, 2024.

pmc-13426208.title: NAT10 inhibition corrects nuclear defects in tau mutant human neurons and extends lifespan in a Drosophila tauopathy model
pmc-13426208.creator: Francesco Paonessa, Bernardo Delarue Bizzini, Tom Campbell, Emily Coode, Jonathan Lam, Ravi Solanki, Richard Butler, James Smith, Catherine M. Davidson, Delphine Larrieu, Andrea H. Brand, Frederick J. Livesey

pmc-13459097.creator: Adam W. Potter, Christy L. Christopoulos, Karl E. Friedl

pmc-13646851.title: Ultra‐Processed Food Consumption and Childhood Allergic Diseases: Increased Risk of Asthma Onset in the SENDO Project
pmc-13646851.creator: O. Galindo, M. J. Goikoetxea, L. Moreno‐Galarraga, L. Argiz, J. M. Moreno‐Villares, Victor de la O, N. Martín‐Calvo
pmc-13646851.description: BackgroundWhile the role of genetic predisposition in asthma and other allergic conditions is well established, the contribution of nutritional patterns is heterogeneous and has been demonstrated in cross‐sectional studies but not in prospective cohorts.MethodsWe analyzed data from 1546 participants enrolled in the SENDO cohort between January 2015 and June 2024. Children aged 4–5 years were prospectively recruited.
